analysis: The only change in landing/src/components/HomeExperience.tsx is an added import of publicLinks from ../content/public-site (head line 13) and the closing-section 'Explore the API' anchor, which now uses publicLinks.docs instead of the hard-coded /developers (head line 1122). This is static marketing-site UI. It does not touch the provider, coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization, encryption keys, prefix-cache storage (T-041), fan helper or token custody. None of the canonical assets (A-001 to A-017) or the trust boundaries TB-002/003/007/009/010/011 are affected. The new href is a plain anchor with no target=_blank or rel handling. Its security depends on the value of publicLinks.docs in ../content/public-site, which is not in the supplied evidence. If that value were attacker-influenced or an unexpected external origin it could matter, but it is a build-time constant in the repo, and nothing supplied shows otherwise. This is an unverified contract rather than a finding. The rest of the file (scroll choreography, network snapshot fetch from /api/network, story carousel) is unchanged. It renders React-escaped values, with no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and the fetched numbers are only formatted via Intl. No regression was identified. A follow-up pass could confirm that publicLinks.docs in public-site is a safe https or relative URL.
